Based on the following evidences, the name “Amonus” is the author of  the SiriusQT RAT (which the following evidence is referring to): 

 

 

The name “Amonus”, is also contained in two PDB references consistent with a Windows development environment: 

 

C:\Users\Rasul\source\repos\Amonus\Sirius-QT\dotnet_loader\obj\Release\NetLoader32.pdb

C:\Users\Rasul\source\repos\Amonus\Sirius-QT\dotnet_loader\obj\Release\NetLoader64.pdb

Observed

  • Author (or co-author) of the SiriusQT RAT, based on the name "Amonus" in the PDB paths of the .NET loader (NetLoader32.pdb, NetLoader64.pdb).

  • Develops on Windows with Visual Studio under the local username "Rasul".

  • Builds in Release configuration, with separate 32-bit and 64-bit loader variants.

Assessed

  • Primarily a malware developer

  • Uses a loader + payload architecture

  • "Amonus" may be an individual or a team, and "Rasul" one of its members (low confidence).

description:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Ylondunor is a low-value forum participant engaged primarily in repetitive message posting to unlock hidden content across multiple topics. Active from March-October 2026 on darkforums[.]me, the user created 8 topics sharing tools and resources (IPTV tools, RATs, configs, subdomain enumeration tools) but demonstrates minimal substantive engagement. The account's 43 messages consist overwhelmingly of identical repeated phrases designed to meet post count requirements, with only 2 messages included in context showing this pattern clearly.

1. User Role and Activities

Ylondunor functions primarily as a content unlocker and resource sharer on darkforums[.]me. The user's activity centers on two main behaviors: creating topics that share various hacking tools, configs, and leaked resources, and participating in other threads with repetitive posting to access hidden content.

The user created 8 topics between October 13-30, 2026, sharing resources including IPTV tools (Hacxx IPTV Player 2, IPTV Tools 1.1.6 Premium_Cracked), malware (EagleRAT v2.5), cracking configs (x200+ Configs for OpenBullet variants), reconnaissance tools (Amass for subdomain enumeration), source code (BTMOB 3.6.3), and leaked data (2 Index of/ a big site, Email Checker). However, the substantive content of these shares is minimal, typically consisting of links to external resources (Telegram channels, pastelink) with hidden content requirements.

The user's participation in 5 other topics (Admin Password Leaks, various crypto exploit threads) shows a pattern of repetitive posting rather than genuine engagement. The statistics indicate 31 messages categorized as "leeching messages," suggesting the majority of the user's 43 total messages follow the pattern observed in the available samples: identical phrases repeated multiple times to unlock content.

2. Profile Overview

Registration: March 1, 2026
Activity Period: March 1 - October 30, 2026 (last active October 30, 2026)
Nickname: Ylondunor (unchanged since registration on October 12, 2026)
Reputation: 0 (unchanged since October 12, 2026)
User Status: DarkForums Members (standard member status, unchanged since October 12, 2026)

The profile shows a basic member account with no reputation development over the 8-month period, indicating minimal community recognition or trust building.

3. Contact Analysis

Own Contacts

The user references a Telegram channel in the "Hacxx IPTV Player 2" topic (October 13, 2026): "hxxps://t[.]me/byprotocol". This appears to be a distribution channel for leaked content, though the exact ownership relationship is unclear from the available context. The user directs others to this channel for accessing "Leaked data," suggesting either ownership or affiliation with this distribution point.

Unknown Contacts

No other contact information or network connections are evident in the available data.

4. Payment Tools

No payment methods, cryptocurrency addresses, or financial transaction details are present in the available message samples or profile data.

5. Geography and Languages

The user communicates in English throughout all visible messages. No personal geographic indicators, location references, or cultural markers are present in the limited message samples. The forum sections activity and topic participation don't reveal specific geographic targeting or regional focus.

6. Timeline and Evolution

March 1, 2026: Account registration
October 12, 2026: First documented post, beginning participation in crypto exploit threads
October 13, 2026: First topic creation (IPTV tools), establishing pattern of tool/resource sharing
October 14-20, 2026: Peak participation period with messages across multiple crypto exploit and leak threads
October 19, 2026: Burst of topic creation (5 topics in one day) covering configs, reconnaissance tools, malware, and source code
October 30, 2026: Final documented activity with database leak topic creation

The timeline shows a concentrated activity burst in mid-October 2026, with the user creating most topics within a week-long period. The gap between registration (March) and first post (October) suggests either lurking behavior or data collection limitations.

7. Activity Statistics Summary

  • Total Messages: 43 (only 2 included in context)
  • Total Topics: 13 (8 created, 5 participated)
  • Activity Period: October 12-30, 2026 (18 days)
  • Topics Created: 8 topics covering tools, configs, malware, and leaks
  • Most Active Sections: World News > Home (8 messages), Leaks > Databases (4 messages), Source Codes > Leaks (4 messages)
  • Categorization: 31 messages flagged as "leeching messages," indicating predominant pattern of low-value posting

The statistics reveal a user focused on quantity over quality, with the vast majority of messages serving to unlock hidden content rather than contribute substantive discussion.

8. Message Content Analysis

The available message samples demonstrate a clear pattern of forum manipulation through repetitive posting. In the "Hacxx IPTV Player 2" topic (October 13, 2026), the user posted an identical phrase 7 times: "Leaked data available here: Hidden Content hxxps://t[.]me/byprotocol". This repetition serves to meet post count requirements for accessing hidden content in other threads.

The second available message (October 30, 2026) in "2 Index of/ a big site !!" follows a similar pattern, directing users to external links (pastelink[.]net) for "ALL DATA" behind hidden content barriers.

The user's topic titles suggest sharing of: - IPTV Tools: Cracked premium IPTV applications - Cracking Configs: 200+ configs for OpenBullet variants (credential stuffing tools) - Reconnaissance Tools: Amass for subdomain enumeration and attack surface discovery - Malware: EagleRAT v2.5 for creating backdoor access - Source Code: BTMOB 3.6.3 complete source with reseller panel - Utilities: Email checker tools - Databases: Index of/ directory listings from compromised sites

However, the actual substantive content of these shares is minimal, primarily consisting of links to external resources rather than detailed descriptions, tutorials, or original content.

9. Detailed Category Analysis

Tools

The user shares various hacking and cracking tools across their created topics:

IPTV Tools (October 13, 2026): Hacxx IPTV Player 2 and IPTV Tools 1.1.6 Premium_Cracked, suggesting interest in pirated streaming services or credential testing against IPTV platforms.

Cracking Configs (October 19, 2026): "x200+ Configs Openbullet, Openbullet 2, SilverBullet 2025" indicates distribution of credential stuffing configurations for automated account checking across various services.

Reconnaissance Tools (October 19, 2026): Amass for "Attack Surface Discovery & Subdomain Enumeration" represents legitimate penetration testing tools that can be used for reconnaissance phases of attacks.

Email Checker (October 19, 2026): Tool for validating email addresses, commonly used in spam campaigns or credential validation workflows.

The tool selection suggests familiarity with the credential stuffing and account checking ecosystem, though no evidence of actual usage or technical expertise is demonstrated in the available messages.

Malware

EagleRAT v2.5 (October 19, 2026): The user shared this remote access trojan described as able to "Create backdoor access points." This represents distribution of malware tools rather than development or deployment evidence. No technical discussion, configuration details, or usage instructions are visible in the available data.

Offers and Services

The user does not advertise services or capabilities for hire. All activity consists of sharing existing tools and resources rather than offering custom work or expertise.

10. Key Operational Characteristics

Low-Effort Content Distribution: The user's operational model centers on minimal-effort sharing of links to external resources (Telegram channels, pastelink) rather than hosting or detailed presentation of materials.

Forum Manipulation: The predominant characteristic is repetitive posting to unlock hidden content, with 31 of 43 messages (72%) categorized as "leeching messages." The visible example shows 7 identical messages in a single post.

Burst Activity Pattern: Concentrated topic creation (5 topics on October 19, 2026) suggests batch uploading or scheduled posting rather than organic engagement.

External Dependency: All shared resources link to external platforms (Telegram, pastelink) rather than direct forum uploads, minimizing the user's exposure while maximizing content access requirements.

Zero Reputation Development: Despite 43 messages over 18 days, the user maintained 0 reputation, indicating no community recognition, vouches, or positive feedback.

11. Patterns and Concerns

Low-Value Activity Patterns

Repetitive Identical Messages: The "Hacxx IPTV Player 2" post demonstrates blatant forum manipulation with 7 identical phrases repeated to inflate post count.

Forum Manipulation Behaviors: The 31 "leeching messages" categorization indicates systematic exploitation of hidden content unlock mechanisms rather than genuine community participation.

Zero Substantive Content: Available messages contain no technical discussion, tutorials, explanations, or original insights—only links and unlock-seeking repetition.

Abnormal Posting Frequency: Creating 5 topics in a single day (October 19) while maintaining minimal message depth suggests automated or batch posting behavior.

Operational Patterns

External Link Dependency: Consistent pattern of directing users to external platforms (Telegram, pastelink) rather than providing direct forum content, which could indicate: - Avoiding forum storage/liability - Driving traffic to controlled channels - Potential monetization through external platforms - Scam risk through unverifiable external links

Topic Abandonment: Created 8 topics with only 1 message each (per statistics), showing no follow-up engagement, support, or community interaction after initial posting.

12. Supporting Evidence

Repetitive Posting Pattern (October 13, 2026, "Hacxx IPTV Player 2"):

"[Repeated 7x] Leaked data available here: Hidden Content hxxps://t[.]me/byprotocol"

This message clearly demonstrates the user's primary operational pattern: repeating identical phrases to meet post count requirements for unlocking hidden content elsewhere on the forum.

External Link Distribution (October 30, 2026, "2 Index of/ a big site !!"):

"Hidden Content ALL DATA: https://pastelink[.]net/nk6ohtyv"

This message shows the consistent pattern of directing users to external platforms for actual content, with minimal context or value-add on the forum itself.

Topic Creation Burst: Statistics show 5 topics created on October 19, 2026 (Configs, Amass, BTMOB, Email Checker, EagleRAT), representing 62.5% of all topics created in a single day, indicating batch posting behavior rather than organic engagement.

Participation Pattern: The user participated in 5 topics with titles suggesting crypto exploits and money-making schemes ("Make $12,000 in 2 days," "Make $2000 in 15 minutes," "Easy money glitch"), with 35 total messages across these threads (81% of all messages), strongly suggesting these were targeted for hidden content unlocking rather than genuine interest.
